meta.description: Structured Phase 1 pathways that connect common young-adult situations to a small set of resource records.

pathways.title: A safe place is needed tonight
pathways.summary: Start with the community entry point that assesses homelessness and immediate housing instability, then use a statewide navigator if the local pathway cannot be reached or does not fit.
documents: Current location and a safe callback number
Any eviction, discharge or termination notice
Names and ages of anyone who must stay together
successCriteria: A screening or assessment is completed
The next contact, location or deadline is clear
The referral outcome is known rather than left open-ended
A backup is identified when no immediate placement is available
pathways.limit: Emergency and shelter capacity is limited. A completed assessment does not guarantee a bed or housing placement. Call 911 when there is immediate danger.

pathways.title: Housing may end within days or weeks
pathways.summary: Confirm the correct prevention or coordinated-entry pathway before the deadline, prepare the documents that establish the housing risk and follow up until eligibility or availability is known.
documents: Lease, occupancy agreement or written housing arrangement
Eviction, termination, discharge or move-out notice
A short timeline of the housing deadline
successCriteria: Eligibility is confirmed or ruled out
Required documents and the application method are known
An alternative is identified if funding or capacity is unavailable
pathways.limit: Many housing programs cannot respond immediately and may require a formal notice, county residency or a specific homelessness definition. Confirm the actual deadline and do not rely on a submitted referral alone.

pathways.title: Several needs are competing at the same time
pathways.summary: Use a navigation or benefits-access entry point to prioritize the most urgent threat, identify which programs are responsible and avoid sending the young adult through a long undifferentiated list.
documents: A short list of the two or three most urgent needs
Photo identification and proof of address, if available
Existing applications, denial notices or caseworker contacts
The deadline connected to each urgent need
successCriteria: The most urgent need is identified first
One responsible program or next action is assigned to each need
Application barriers and required documents are identified
A follow-up date is set for unresolved referrals
pathways.limit: Navigation can reduce confusion and administrative burden, but it cannot create service capacity. Document when the correct resource exists but is unavailable so the gap is not mistaken for a search failure.
